root_cause: The focus trap is not activated because the offcanvas instance is configured with scroll=true (via data-bs-scroll="true"), which prevents activation of the focus trap in the show method.
repair_strategy: Modify the offcanvas show method to always activate the focus trap when the offcanvas is shown, regardless of the scroll setting, ensuring keyboard focus remains trapped inside the offcanvas panel.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the help panel is opened, pressing Tab will cycle focus within the panel (between the help text and close button) and not move focus to underlying page elements.
functional_risks: Activating the focus trap regardless of the scroll setting may affect users who expect to interact with page background while the offcanvas is open, but focus trapping does not interfere with scrolling.
There is a low risk of unexpected focus behavior if other scripts manage focus concurrently, but the offcanvas already manages its own focus trap lifecycle.
verification_requirements: After opening the help panel, the first Tab press moves focus to #help-close.
The second Tab press keeps focus inside the panel (either loops back to #help-close or to another focusable element inside).
Closing the panel restores focus to the trigger button as per existing behavior.
The panel continues to allow scrolling when data-bs-scroll="true" is set.
